q: So, I’ve been a bit stressed lately cause I felt like there is a ton to do and I’m not prepared. I haven’t decorated the room, it looks like a mix a match furniture in there. I usually think and research a lot before buying anything, which makes it a lot more work.
cx: At 30 weeks, no shower planned, most small items still to buy.

q: Now we are in Ikea, and everything I touch he starts to say either we don’t need it, or it’s too early to buy it (I was picking up some baby proofing stuff) or constantly questioning why do you need that.
cx: A frugal couple's nursery shopping trip ends with her in tears in the kids section.

q: I feel like he doesn’t understand how much work it’s gonna be when baby is here.
cx: Her husband says they can buy things after the birth.

q: We decided to skip the baby shower just because we don’t know many poeple, and don’t have anyone who can plan for me.
cx: Why she is buying the remaining items herself.

q: It's not about the stuff itself, it's about ownership and agency. I want to build this life/family ourselves, not have it built for us and controlled by my in laws. I'm also worried that accepting all of this help will set a precedent for future decisions like parenting choices, holidays, routines, education etc etc
cx: At 9 weeks, wealthy in-laws down the street push to pay for a kitchen and nursery.

q: Tonight my FIL starts going off "well I'll come over and do xyz" and I nonchalantly said "ohhh yea, it's so early so the focus right now is just staying healthy and we'll work on the house projects later" but he just kept pushing.
cx: Her father-in-law presses on nursery projects at 9 weeks.

q: Everyone says use your partner to help, but mine is never consistently here to help. Up until 2 weeks ago he worked away regularly during the week.
cx: At 33 weeks with her second, working full time with a 22-month-old.

q: When I’m struggling to bend down to pick up toys, feeling pelvic floor pressure from not being able to rest and chasing a toddler - I think how much I wish my Partner showed up for us more. It’s compounding. I’m resentful.
cx: Late in a second pregnancy, mostly alone with the toddler.

q: To be honest we didn’t plan number 2 this close but I’m excited to meet her and I’ll have a year of paid mat leave. I know our toddler is going to be very caring. I’m just so anxious about the lack of support as I’m getting more heavily pregnant and my partner hasn’t done one thing to help prepare for the baby.
cx: Close-spaced second baby; a year of paid leave but little help at home.

q: My in-laws live overseas and my husband wants them to stay with us for 3+ weeks during my pregnancy. I’ve asked for some space because I’ve never been pregnant before and I know I get overwhelmed easily.
cx: First pregnancy; husband wants his overseas parents for a long stay.

q: And I totally get wanting to have a relationship with your child but does it have to be at my most vulnerable state? If they came after a few months after I’ve healed up I feel that should be fine
cx: She has asked overseas in-laws not to stay until six months after the birth.

q: They want to come more while I’m pregnant than when the baby is born 🙃 we just saw visited them a few weeks ago and stayed together for 4 weeks and it was long and tough
cx: On the in-laws' wish to stay during the pregnancy itself.

q: he said "so theres 0 studies showing if theres long term benefits?" Never thought id have to cite my sources and debate over my nipples.
cx: Almost six weeks postpartum, her fiancé argues against switching to formula.

q: Mind you He isn't working hes on paid paternity leave.
cx: She does every night alone; he compares her strain to his job while on paid leave (US state leave).

q: If I walk in the door with baby, I don’t exist until I don’t know when. I might as well not have came. And trying to talk to people? Forget it. They’re too interested in baby to pay any attention.
cx: A first-time mother on relatives who fuss over the baby and ignore her.

q: we live in a small townhome and I am already trying to juggle hosting MIL and mom and cats. this family is expecting to stay with us. I tried talking to one of the grandaunts but she brushes off everything I said and claims the early stages is when family is needed most.
cx: Expectant father: mother-in-law flying from Singapore, his mother, and now distant relatives planning stays around the due date.

q: i have hired cleaners for my wife. I plan to meal prep for us or hire a meal delivery service.
cx: His own plan for the first weeks, before the relatives' visits.

q: please help me get the message across to these extended family members that we are not saying don’t come, we’re saying please give us time. I am perplexed that the elderly matriarchs who have gone through pregnancies are the ones dismissing everything I am trying to say.
cx: Asking how to word a delay to relatives they barely know.

q: Right now he is judging me for being tired and sick a lot of the time. I told him today its just the rollercoaster of hormones and he said "you think this is hard, wait till you have a baby"
cx: Newly pregnant, working two jobs; her elderly father lives with the couple.

q: “What are your cravings? Oh you can’t be eating fried food! That is not good for you! You need to be eating healthier!”
cx: Her father-in-law's comments at about 6 weeks, before her first OB visit.

q: “Are you sure you’re only 6 weeks because you look like you’re further along? I hope you don’t find that offensive.”
cx: Another of her father-in-law's weekend remarks.
